statement: For every infinite cardinal nu and group H of cardinality at most nu, there is a fixed group E_H of cardinality at most nu containing H such that every relative presentation over H with integral exponent map an isomorphism, at most two full new-variable supports per relator, and nonzero exponent on every occurring new variable admits a homomorphism to E_H extending the chosen embedding of H. Consequently, a two-dimensional classifying model with countable H1,H2 and this support condition outside countable exceptional cell sets has a countable quotient detecting every nonidentity element.
depends_on: A.19 finite-nonsingular-equation closure and homology-core construction
Finite-support graph analysis of the actual exponent isomorphism
manuscript_pages_settled: PROMPT Part A3(iii): anchored two-variable Camm-type construction cannot give no-countable-image groups with the specified small homology
notes: The full-word support requirement includes zero-exponent occurrences and is stronger than merely bounding nonzero entries of the exponent matrix. Components of the matrix graph are grounded trees or nonsingular unicyclic components; all equations solve by finite distance from a ground or finite cycle. The D agent independently checked the graph and recursion argument, and the A agent independently audited the complete manuscript with no correction needed. This is an exact obstruction for the stated construction class, without a general conclusion for three-variable or zero-exponent-word modifications.
